newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: INTERVIEW-Bangladesh to promote bond market.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Bangladesh to promote bond market.

text.p: Bangladesh will allow merchant banks to operate and create a bond market, in a bid to expand the country's capital market and boost investment, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) chief said.

"We are trying to establish a bond market. We are looking for technical assistance to develop the framework for setting up the bond market in the country," Haroonur Rashid, SEC chairman told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
Rashid said the SEC would also aim to bring treasury bonds into the market.
"The SEC is in consultations with the central bank on the possiblity of establishing discount houses to bring the treasury bonds into the market."
"The investors will then have more choice. The people have risk in dealing with ordinary shares," he said.
Rashid said the government would also allow private mutual funds to operate soon.
"The registration for floating such funds is almost in (the) final stage. If you want to create depth you have to have more financial instruments in the market," he said.
Rashid said the SEC recently ordered stock dealers to give up their directorship of listed companies with a view to stopping the "possibility of manipulations."
He said: "It's necessary to remove conflicts of interest," and ensure better transparency.
Rashid rejected World Bank criticism that the SEC was responsible for recent upheavals in the capital market, saying the SEC made sincere efforts to make people aware of erratic market behavior.
He said the SEC warned people through television and newspapers about the risks involved in trading shares of companies with poor financial records.
Thousands of retail investors sparked a steep rally in the stock market last year, soon after general elections in June brought Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to power.
The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) benchmark index jumped to the 3,600 level by October from less than 1,000 in June.
The market, however, has suffered a long run of bearishness since November. The index closed at 1,804.09 on Thursday.
Stock market players have blamed manipulation and malpractice for the sharp swings in the index.
Rashid said: "In fact we were not late in taking action. The traders mostly ignored our warnings."
He said the SEC had asked the DSE to impose circuit breakers or limits on share price fluctuations twice to cool down the market.
"Brokers were not even ready for such an upsurge. Even in the most sophisticated market, rises and falls take place. It's driven by a lot of speculation," he said.

Rashid said the SEC would launch a public awareness campaign to give financial information about companies. Documentary films will be shown to the public on how to invest in the capital market, he said.
